Your first X-ray spectrum

Simulate a small crystalline target and compare PXR + CBS with bremsstrahlung.

Setup

This example uses 30 keV electrons incident upon a 100 nm HOPG slab. Its small trial counts keep it CPU-friendly; the curves are only illustrative. The sampled electron histories do not represent a physical bunch population.

data.text/markdown:
Interpretation

PXR and CBS are combined here because their amplitudes interfere. Their line structure differs from the broad bremsstrahlung continuum. Plot each component on its native photon-energy grid; adding array entries by index would mix different energies. The vertical axis is source spectral density per incident electron, per eV, per steradian: it is neither physical beam flux nor acquired counts. Low history counts can leave noisy features and empty bins. Try doubling the history counts, then change only the target thickness. Keep a record of the resolved seed when comparing configurations; different backends need not produce identical random trajectories. Continue to notebook 02 to separate source yields from beam-current-scaled photon rates. Notebook 03 predicts vacuum line energies; the results how-to covers saved checkpoints. See model limitations and validation status before interpreting these small-sample results quantitatively.
